# std.hash

Hashing and the hash tables built on it: `Hash`, `HashMap` and `HashSet`. A table finds a key by its salted `hash` and compares keys with `==`, in \(O(1)\) expected per lookup, insert and remove. Walking one has no defined order, so neither is `Show` (R10.3.8); `Map` and `Set` are the ordered spelling (lib/containers.md §2.8).

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Hash`, `HashMap`, `HashSet`, `splitmix64`.

## `trait Hash`

A value's 64-bit hash: equal values hash equal.

## `struct HashMap<K, V>`

A hash table from `K` to `V` whatever the program observes: C++ `unordered_map`, Python `dict`, Rust `HashMap`.

- `fn new() -> HashMap<K, V>` — \(O(1)\); An empty map; `HashMap(pairs)` builds one from `(key, value)` pairs.

## `struct HashSet<T>`

A hash set of `T` whatever the program observes: C++ `unordered_set`, Python `set`, Rust `HashSet`.

- `fn new() -> HashSet<T>` — \(O(1)\); An empty set; `HashSet(xs)` builds one from the elements of `xs`.

## Functions

- `fn splitmix64(x: U64) -> U64` — \(O(1)\); SplitMix64: mixes the 64 bits of `x` so that inputs close together land far apart.
